intervention_dose: 300 mg PO BID continuous
indication: HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer with germline BRCA1/2 mutation (TNBC or HR+; up to 2 prior chemo lines)
population_detail: Germline BRCA1/2 carriers; 50% TNBC, 50% HR+; ECOG 0-1; prior anthracycline and taxane required; up to 2 prior chemotherapy lines for metastatic disease.
comparator: Physician's choice single-agent chemotherapy (capecitabine, vinorelbine, eribulin)
safety_summary: Grade 3+ AE rate 36.6% (olaparib) vs 50.5% (chemo). Discontinuation 4.9% vs 7.7%. Anemia is the dominant olaparib AE; nausea and fatigue common all-grade.
notes: Pivotal registrational RCT supporting FDA approval of olaparib in germline-BRCA HER2-negative mBC. Patient is a textbook fit if BRCA1 resolves to germline; somatic-only is off-label for the breast indication.

intervention_dose: 1 mg PO daily continuous
indication: Locally advanced or metastatic HER2-negative breast cancer with germline BRCA1/2 mutation
population_detail: Germline BRCA1/2 carriers; 45% TNBC, 55% HR+; ECOG 0-2; prior taxane or anthracycline required unless contraindicated; up to 3 prior chemo lines.
comparator: Physician's choice chemotherapy (capecitabine, eribulin, gemcitabine, vinorelbine)

outcomes.name: HR_OS
outcomes.notes: 57% events at primary analysis; OS not significantly improved

safety_summary: Hematologic toxicity is the dominant signal: grade 3-4 anemia ~39%, thrombocytopenia ~15%, neutropenia ~21%. Hematologic G3-4 55% (talazoparib) vs 38% (chemo); non-hematologic G3 32% vs 38%.
notes: Pivotal registrational RCT for talazoparib in germline-BRCA HER2-negative mBC. Choice between olaparib and talazoparib usually rests on hematologic-toxicity tolerance — talazoparib has substantially higher anemia rates.

intervention_dose: 300 mg PO BID for 12 months
indication: High-risk early-stage HER2-negative breast cancer with germline BRCA1/2 mutation (adjuvant)
population_detail: Germline BRCA1/2 carriers; high-risk early breast cancer (TNBC or HR+); residual disease after neoadjuvant chemo OR pT2/pN1 after adjuvant chemo.

outcomes.name: HR_DFS
outcomes.notes: invasive DFS; primary endpoint at primary analysis

safety_summary: Adjuvant olaparib was well tolerated: G3+ AE rate ~24.5% vs 11.3% placebo; MDS/AML signal not elevated.
notes: OlympiA is the adjuvant standard for germline-BRCA early breast cancer. Patient is de novo M1, not adjuvant, so the label does not apply. Included for evidence-base completeness on the BRCA1 PARP-inhibitor axis; supports post-consolidation olaparib if oligometastatic conversion is pursued.

intervention_dose: Veliparib 120 mg PO BID days 1-7 + carboplatin AUC 6 d3 + paclitaxel 80 mg/m^2 d3, 10, 17 q21d
indication: HER2-negative advanced breast cancer with germline BRCA1/2 mutation
population_detail: Germline BRCA1/2 carriers; HER2-neg locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer; ECOG 0-2; up to 2 prior chemo lines, including 1 prior platinum allowed if 6+ months prior.

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: vs 74.1% control — no ORR difference; benefit was durability

safety_summary: Hematologic toxicity dominates: G3+ neutropenia ~81%, thrombocytopenia 40%, anemia 42%. Veliparib added modest thrombocytopenia incrementally; no new safety signals.
notes: PFS improvement did not translate into OS benefit at final analysis. Veliparib was never FDA-approved in breast cancer; the regimen anchors the BRCA-mut platinum/PARP-i combination concept but is not commercially available. Useful as evidence base; not directly prescribable.

intervention_dose: Paclitaxel 80 mg/m^2 weekly x12 + carboplatin AUC 6 q3w x4 + veliparib 50 mg PO BID (or placebo) — then AC
indication: Stage II-III triple-negative breast cancer, neoadjuvant
population_detail: Treatment-naive stage II-III TNBC; BRCA-mut and BRCA-WT both eligible; 3-arm trial.
comparator: Paclitaxel + carboplatin + veliparib-placebo (arm B); paclitaxel + double-placebo (arm C)
p_value: <0.0001 (Arm A vs C); 0.36 (Arm A vs B)
safety_summary: Hematologic toxicity heavy across arms: G3-4 neutropenia 56%, anemia 29%, thrombocytopenia 12% (entire 628-pt safety population). Veliparib did not improve pCR over carboplatin alone.
notes: Patient is M1 not stage II-III, so neoadjuvant regimen does not directly apply. Included because BrighTNess shows the platinum component drives the pCR gain, not veliparib — informs how to weight platinum vs PARP-i in the 1L systemic regimen for this BRCA1 patient.

indication: Stage II-III triple-negative breast cancer, neoadjuvant
population_detail: Same 634-patient cohort, 4.5-yr median follow-up
comparator: Paclitaxel + carboplatin (arm B); paclitaxel alone (arm C)

outcomes.name: HR_EFS
outcomes.subgroup: Arm A (veliparib+carbo+pacli) vs Arm C (pacli alone)

outcomes.name: HR_EFS
outcomes.subgroup: Arm B (carbo+pacli) vs Arm C (pacli alone)

safety_summary: No new long-term safety signals; no excess second malignancies (MDS/AML) with carboplatin or veliparib over the 4.5-yr window.

toxicities.notes: no excess with carbo or veliparib

notes: Long-term follow-up confirms that adding carboplatin (not veliparib) drives the EFS gain. Decision-relevant for choosing platinum-containing 1L systemic backbone in a BRCA-mut patient.

intervention_dose: 300 mg PO daily continuous (later weight-based)
indication: Germline BRCA1/2-mutated HER2-negative advanced breast cancer
population_detail: Germline BRCA1/2 carriers; HER2-neg locally advanced or metastatic; up to 2 prior chemo lines; ECOG 0-2.
comparator: Physician's choice chemotherapy (eribulin, capecitabine, vinorelbine, gemcitabine)

outcomes.name: HR_PFS
outcomes.notes: central PFS (primary); halted at interim for futility

safety_summary: Niraparib AE profile dominated by hematologic toxicity: G3 thrombocytopenia, neutropenia, anemia each in 15-30% of patients; characteristic platelet decline early.
notes: Trial halted for futility on central review, though local PFS suggested benefit — the central-vs-local discordance is the published interpretation caveat. Niraparib is not FDA-approved in breast cancer; off-label only and likely to face payer pushback vs labeled olaparib/talazoparib.

intervention_dose: Niraparib 200 mg PO daily + pembrolizumab 200 mg IV q3w
indication: Advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer
population_detail: Advanced TNBC; BRCA-mut (n=15) and BRCA-WT (n=27) both eligible; up to 2 prior cytotoxic lines.

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: the headline number that supports the BRCA-mut TIL-rich phenotype rationale

safety_summary: G3+ anemia 18%, thrombocytopenia 15%, fatigue 7%. Immune-related AEs in 15% of pts; G3 irAEs 4%.
notes: The 47% ORR in BRCA-mut TNBC is the foundational chemo-free PARP-i + ICI signal. Patient's BRCA1 + TIL-rich + TMB-H profile is the canonical TOPACIO responder phenotype; niraparib off-label in breast cancer.

intervention_dose: Olaparib 300 mg PO BID + durvalumab 1500 mg IV q4w (4-wk olaparib lead-in)
indication: Germline BRCA-mutated HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer
population_detail: Germline BRCA1/2 carriers; HER2-neg mBC; up to 2 prior chemo lines; ECOG 0-1.
design: Single-arm phase 1/2 basket expansion (MEDIOLA breast cohort)
safety_summary: G3+ AEs 32% (11/34); commonest anemia 12%, neutropenia 9%, pancreatitis 6%. Three discontinuations for AE; no treatment-related deaths.
notes: Small but mechanistically clean PARP-i + PD-L1 cohort in germline-BRCA HER2-neg mBC. Supports an olaparib + durvalumab maintenance strategy after platinum-containing 1L induction; regimen is off-label outside of trials.

intervention_dose: Olaparib 300 mg PO BID +/- durvalumab 1500 mg IV q4w as maintenance after platinum induction
indication: Platinum-pretreated advanced TNBC, maintenance after platinum response
population_detail: Advanced TNBC with SD/CR/PR on 1L-2L platinum chemo; HRD-positive / BRCA-mut enriched but not required; randomized 1:1.
safety_summary: Tolerable maintenance profile; most common AEs (>30%) were nausea, fatigue, anemia in olaparib arm; combo added decreased appetite, vomiting, cough. G3-4 events scattered (<5% per term).
notes: Chemo-free PARP-i + ICI maintenance after platinum induction; design template for a defensible off-trial regimen in this patient given her BRCA1 + TIL-rich + TMB-H phenotype. Requires prior platinum, so not 1L-enrollable.

intervention_label: Carboplatin (vs docetaxel) in BRCA-mutated mTNBC — TNT trial
intervention_dose: Carboplatin AUC 6 IV q21d
indication: Metastatic or recurrent locally advanced TNBC or BRCA1/2-mutant breast cancer
population_detail: Unselected advanced TNBC (376 pts); 43 patients with germline BRCA1/2 mutations identified by prospective biomarker analysis.
outcome: ORR overall and in BRCA-mut subgroup
median_dor_or_pfs: mPFS BRCA-mut 6.8 mo carbo vs 4.4 mo doce (HR 0.44)

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: vs 34.0% doce, p=0.66 — no difference unselected

safety_summary: Carboplatin and docetaxel both well-tolerated as single agents at standard doses; AE profiles differ predictably — carboplatin myelosuppression, docetaxel neuropathy/edema/alopecia.

toxicities.notes: carboplatin arm; lower than combo regimens

notes: TNT is the platinum-vs-taxane RCT establishing that BRCA-mut TNBC has double the carboplatin ORR vs docetaxel (68% vs 33%) — the foundational platinum-sensitivity data in BRCA1-mut TNBC. Anchors a carboplatin-containing 1L backbone for this patient.

intervention_label: Carboplatin added to neoadjuvant paclitaxel + AC
intervention_dose: Paclitaxel 80 mg/m^2 weekly x12 +/- carboplatin AUC 6 q3w x4, then dose-dense AC
indication: Stage II-III triple-negative breast cancer, neoadjuvant
population_detail: Clinical stage II-III previously untreated TNBC; BRCA status not stratified at enrollment.
safety_summary: Carboplatin increased G3-4 neutropenia and thrombocytopenia roughly 2-fold over paclitaxel-AC alone; bevacizumab added hypertension and bleeding.
notes: Neoadjuvant trial in stage II-III TNBC, not metastatic. Included because it established the pCR gain from adding carboplatin to neoadjuvant chemo in unselected TNBC — supports a carboplatin-containing 1L systemic backbone for this M1 patient given her BRCA1 status.

intervention_dose: 10 mg/kg IV days 1, 8 q21d
indication: Pretreated metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (>=2 prior lines including a taxane)
population_detail: mTNBC after >=2 prior lines in advanced setting, must include a taxane; brain-mets cohort separate.
comparator: Treatment of physician's choice (eribulin, capecitabine, gemcitabine, vinorelbine)
safety_summary: G3+ neutropenia 51%, diarrhea 10%, anemia 8%; G3 febrile neutropenia 6%. Discontinuation for AE 4.7%. Characteristic AE: neutropenia + diarrhea from the SN-38 payload.
notes: Pivotal RCT supporting FDA approval of sacituzumab govitecan in 2L+ mTNBC. Patient is 1L-treatment-naive so not directly enrollable; anchors the basal-like/TROP2-ADC axis for the likely 2L option after progression on 1L ICI + chemo.

indication: Pretreated metastatic TNBC (final database lock + HER2/TROP2 expression subgroups)
outcome: Final OS analysis; HER2 / TROP2 expression subgroups
median_dor_or_pfs: Final mOS 11.8 vs 6.9 mo; mPFS 4.8 vs 1.7 mo (ITT)
safety_summary: Long-term safety consistent with primary analysis; no cumulative neutropenia signal. TROP2 expression did not gate benefit — efficacy seen across TROP2 H-score subgroups.
notes: Final ASCENT readout confirms durability of SG OS benefit and shows efficacy is preserved across TROP2 expression strata — a useful counter to selection arguments for biomarker-restricted use.

intervention_dose: SG 10 mg/kg IV days 1, 8 q21d + pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w
indication: Previously untreated PD-L1+ (CPS >=10) metastatic TNBC, 1L
population_detail: PD-L1 CPS >=10 by 22C3; treatment-naive in advanced setting; ECOG 0-1; both BRCA-mut and -WT eligible.
safety_summary: Combination safety dominated by SG-related neutropenia and diarrhea plus pembrolizumab irAEs; no unexpected interactions vs SG monotherapy in ASCENT.

toxicities.notes: SG+pembro arm; approximate from interim reporting

notes: ASCENT-04 supports a 1L SG + pembrolizumab regimen for PD-L1 CPS >=10 mTNBC. Pivotal readout from 2025 presentations; full publication is the next decision-relevant pivot, currently in press at the time of writing — confirm citation when available.

intervention_dose: 6 mg/kg IV q3w
indication: Previously untreated locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic TNBC ineligible for PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors (e.g. PD-L1 CPS <10)
population_detail: 1L mTNBC, ICI-ineligible (PD-L1 CPS <10 by 22C3 or prior anti-PD-1 in early setting <6 mo prior); ECOG 0-1.
comparator: Investigator's choice chemo (paclitaxel, nab-paclitaxel, carboplatin, capecitabine, eribulin)
safety_summary: Dato-DXd safety profile dominated by stomatitis, ocular events, and ILD/pneumonitis; G3+ TRAE ~35%, fewer hematologic events than chemo arm.
notes: TROPION-Breast02 is the 1L PD-L1-low / ICI-ineligible TNBC pivotal for Dato-DXd. If patient's PD-L1 CPS returns <10 she lands in this trial's target population. Anchors near-term label expansion.

intervention_dose: Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV q3w + investigator-choice chemo (nab-paclitaxel, paclitaxel, or gemcitabine/carboplatin)
indication: Previously untreated locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic TNBC
population_detail: 1L mTNBC; PD-L1 stratified by 22C3 CPS; ECOG 0-1; primary endpoint in CPS >=10 subgroup.
safety_summary: G3+ AE rate 68% pembro+chemo vs 67% chemo alone; immune-mediated AEs additive but expected; characteristic G3+ irAEs hypothyroidism, hepatitis, pneumonitis at single-digit rates.
notes: Pivotal trial driving FDA approval of pembrolizumab + chemo for 1L mTNBC CPS >=10. Patient is treatment-naive with TIL-rich and TMB-H phenotype; PD-L1 CPS is pending and gates the regimen.

intervention_dose: Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV q3w + chemo
indication: Previously untreated mTNBC, PD-L1 CPS >=10 final OS
population_detail: Same 847-patient cohort; final OS analysis at 44-mo median follow-up.
safety_summary: Long-term safety consistent with primary readout. G3+ AEs 68.1% pembro+chemo vs 66.9% placebo+chemo; treatment-related deaths 0.4% vs 0%.
notes: Final OS readout confirming 7-mo median OS gain in CPS >=10. The defining survival evidence for 1L pembrolizumab + chemo in mTNBC.

intervention_dose: Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w during neoadj + adj phases on paclitaxel/carboplatin then AC backbone
indication: Stage II-III triple-negative breast cancer, neoadjuvant
population_detail: Stage II-III TNBC; PD-L1-agnostic; ECOG 0-1.
safety_summary: G3+ TRAE 78% in pembro arm vs 73% in placebo arm; immune-related AEs additive — endocrinopathy and skin-mediated events most common.
notes: Neoadjuvant TNBC trial; the patient is M1 not stage II-III so the regimen is not directly applicable. Included because the TIL-3+/TMB-14 phenotype matches the subgroup with the largest pCR gain, which reinforces the case for a KEYNOTE-355-style 1L ICI+chemo regimen in metastatic disease.

intervention_dose: Atezolizumab 840 mg IV days 1, 15 + nab-paclitaxel 100 mg/m^2 days 1, 8, 15 q28d
indication: Previously untreated metastatic TNBC
population_detail: 1L mTNBC; primary endpoints in ITT and PD-L1 IC >=1% by SP142.
outcome: PFS overall and in PD-L1+ subgroup
safety_summary: G3+ AEs comparable across arms; treatment discontinuation 15.9% (atezo) vs 8.2% (placebo). Characteristic irAEs hypothyroidism and pneumonitis.
notes: IMpassion130 led to the original accelerated approval of atezo+nab-paclitaxel in PD-L1 SP142 IC >=1% mTNBC; the indication was voluntarily withdrawn in 2021 after IMpassion131 failed to confirm benefit. Kept as historical anchor — the patient cannot access this regimen in the US.

intervention_dose: Atezolizumab 840 mg IV days 1, 15 + paclitaxel 90 mg/m^2 days 1, 8, 15 q28d
indication: Previously untreated metastatic TNBC
population_detail: 1L mTNBC; randomized 2:1 atezo+paclitaxel vs placebo+paclitaxel; 45% PD-L1+.
safety_summary: Safety consistent with IMpassion130; G3+ AE rates comparable across arms.
notes: Negative confirmatory trial: paclitaxel solvent (vs nab-paclitaxel) is the leading published hypothesis for the IMpassion130/131 discordance. The failure triggered the US withdrawal of atezolizumab in mTNBC. Included as the evidence anchor for why the patient should be steered to the pembrolizumab + chemo backbone rather than atezolizumab.

intervention_label: Pembrolizumab monotherapy in TMB-H solid tumors
intervention_dose: 200 mg IV q3w
indication: Advanced solid tumors with TMB-H (>=10 mut/Mb by FoundationOne CDx)
population_detail: Prospectively-defined TMB-H cohort across 10 tumor types; no prior anti-PD-(L)1; failed >=1 prior line; included anal, biliary, cervical, endometrial, mesothelioma, neuroendocrine, salivary, small-cell lung, thyroid, vulvar — breast was NOT in the basket.
design: Single-arm, prospectively-defined TMB-H cohort within multi-cohort phase 2 (KEYNOTE-158)
safety_summary: G3-5 TRAE rate ~15% in the safety population; 1 treatment-related death from pneumonitis. Profile typical of pembrolizumab monotherapy.
notes: KEYNOTE-158 supports the tumor-agnostic pembrolizumab indication for TMB-H >=10 mut/Mb on FoundationOne CDx. Breast cancer was NOT in the original basket — application to this patient is cross-tumor extrapolation. Label requires prior progression and no satisfactory alternatives; not yet applicable in 1L.

intervention_dose: Capivasertib 400 mg PO BID days 2-5 weekly + paclitaxel 80 mg/m^2 IV weekly
indication: Previously untreated metastatic TNBC
population_detail: 1L mTNBC; dual primary endpoint in overall and PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered (30.7%) populations; ECOG 0-1.
outcome: OS overall and AKT-pathway-altered populations (dual primary)
safety_summary: G3+ diarrhea the dominant capivasertib-specific AE; hyperglycemia and rash also characteristic. Manageable with dose modification; no new safety signals.
notes: Negative phase 3 OS readout in TNBC, including in the PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered stratum that would have been the patient's most likely benefit subgroup. Decision-relevant evidence against off-label capivasertib + paclitaxel in 1L mTNBC.

intervention_dose: Adavosertib 175 mg PO BID days 1-3, 8-10, 15-17 + cisplatin 75 mg/m^2 IV q21d
indication: Metastatic triple-negative breast cancer, 1L-2L
population_detail: mTNBC; 1L or 2L; BRCA-mut and BRCA-WT both eligible; TP53 status not stratified.

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: primary endpoint; pre-specified threshold >30% not met

safety_summary: Diarrhea (21% G3+), nausea, neutropenia, fatigue dominate; G3+ TRAE 53%. Combination poorly tolerated at protocol doses.
notes: Adavosertib + cisplatin missed the pre-specified 30% ORR threshold in mTNBC and no genomic correlate (including TP53) predicted response. Tempers the WEE1-inhibitor rationale for TP53-mut TNBC; remains experimental, trial-only.

intervention_dose: Olaparib 300 mg PO BID continuous + ceralasertib 160 mg PO days 1-7 of 28-day cycle
indication: Metastatic TNBC with HRR mutation stratification
population_detail: mTNBC; stratified BRCA-mut vs HRR-mut non-BRCA vs HRR-WT; up to 2 prior chemo lines.
safety_summary: Hematologic toxicity additive — anemia and thrombocytopenia heightened with the combination. Adavosertib arm closed early for toxicity.
notes: VIOLETTE is the dedicated PARPi + DDR combination phase 2 in mTNBC. Both combinations failed to beat olaparib monotherapy; adavosertib arm closed for toxicity. Decision-relevant evidence against routinely combining ATR/WEE1 with olaparib in BRCA1-mut TNBC outside of trials.

intervention_label: Pembrolizumab + olaparib maintenance after pembro+chemo induction
intervention_dose: Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV q3w + olaparib 300 mg PO BID maintenance
indication: Locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic TNBC after induction with 1L pembrolizumab + chemo
population_detail: mTNBC with SD/CR/PR on 4-6 cycles of pembro+chemo induction; HRR-mut stratified.
safety_summary: Pembro+olaparib 84% G3+ TRAE vs pembro+chemo 96% — combo regimen better tolerated than continued chemo. Anemia dominant in olaparib arm.
notes: Overall negative; BRCA1/2-mut subgroup signal (HR ~0.70) supports the strategy of pembro+chemo induction followed by olaparib-based maintenance for BRCA1-mut patients. Hypothesis-generating, not practice-changing.

intervention_label: Stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (SABR) for oligometastatic disease
intervention_dose: SABR per lesion-specific protocols (typically 3-5 fractions) + standard palliative care
indication: Controlled primary solid tumor with 1-5 metastatic lesions (mixed histologies, including breast)
population_detail: Multiple primary sites; 18% breast; 1-5 oligometastases; controlled primary.
safety_summary: G2+ AE rate 29% (SABR) vs 9% (control); 3 treatment-related deaths in the SABR arm (4.5%) vs none in control — important toxicity signal for any oligometastatic ablation discussion.
notes: Foundational randomized evidence for SABR consolidation in mixed-tumor oligometastases. Patient is breast-only-liver oligomet (single 1.5 cm lesion); SABR-COMET is a small phase 2 across multiple tumor types — the OS HR is encouraging but NRG-BR002 in breast-specific cohort tempers extrapolation.

intervention_label: SBRT or surgical resection of oligometastatic breast cancer (NRG-BR002)
intervention_dose: SBRT per RTOG guidelines or surgical resection of all metastatic lesions
indication: Newly oligometastatic breast cancer (1-4 metastases) of any subtype, on standard systemic therapy
population_detail: Breast-specific cohort; 1-4 oligometastases; on standard systemic therapy; randomized to add consolidation vs continue systemic alone.
outcome: Safety (primary); PFS phase IIR readout negative at SABCS 2024

outcomes.name: HR_PFS
outcomes.notes: favors continued systemic therapy arm; phase IIR analysis

safety_summary: SBRT well-tolerated; no excess high-grade toxicity vs systemic therapy alone in the published safety analysis. Phase IIR PFS readout did not favor consolidation.

toxicities.notes: SBRT arm; approximate from safety analysis

notes: Breast-specific oligometastatic consolidation trial — phase IIR PFS readout was negative for consolidation (HR ~1.31), tempering the curative-intent framing for this de novo oligometastatic patient. Decision-relevant evidence against routine SBRT/resection over systemic therapy alone; biology-driven case-by-case board discussions still continue.

intervention_label: Early locoregional therapy of intact primary in de novo stage IV breast cancer
intervention_dose: Surgery (mastectomy or breast-conserving) + radiotherapy + axillary management, layered on systemic therapy
indication: De novo stage IV breast cancer with intact primary tumor, no progression after 4-8 mo of optimal systemic therapy
population_detail: Stage IV intact primary; 50% HR+/HER2-, 29% HER2+, 10% TNBC, 11% other; bone-only 31%, viscera-only 26%, both 27%; median age 55.
safety_summary: Surgical and radiotherapy AEs as expected; locoregional disease control was higher in the surgery arm (3-yr LR recurrence 10.2% vs 25.6%) — symptom relief, not survival, is the value proposition.
notes: Definitive RCT showing no OS benefit from resecting an intact primary in de novo M1 breast cancer. The patient's locoregional control may still warrant local therapy if symptomatic — the trial does not say no, it says no OS benefit. Decision-relevant counter-evidence to routine surgical consolidation.

intervention_dose: ZEN-3694 oral daily + talazoparib 1 mg PO daily
indication: Metastatic TNBC without germline BRCA1/2 mutations
population_detail: mTNBC; germline BRCA1/2-WT required; up to 3 prior lines; MYC-driven / basal-like enriched.
safety_summary: BET inhibitor class effects: thrombocytopenia, fatigue, nausea. Talazoparib contributes anemia. Manageable with dose modification per the phase 1b portion.

toxicities.notes: BET-i class effect; approximate from abstract

notes: ASCO 2022 abstract only; full publication pending. The trial restricted to BRCA-WT TNBC, so it does NOT directly apply to this patient (BRCA1-mut). Included to anchor the BET-inhibitor evidence base for the MYC-amplification axis — patient is BRCA1-mut so this regimen is not enrollable for her.

exclusion_reason: Patient is HER2 fully negative (HER2 0 by IHC implied by 'HER2-negative' on profile); DESTINY-Breast04 enrolled HER2-LOW (IHC 1+ or 2+/FISH-) — patient does not qualify unless reflex IHC confirms HER2-low status. Per profile.json the HER2-0 vs HER2-low distinction is not specified; flagged as not applicable pending confirmation.
notes: DESTINY-Breast04 established T-DXd in HER2-low mBC. Patient documented HER2 'negative' without specifying IHC 0 vs 1+/2+. If reflex confirms HER2-low (1+ or 2+/FISH-), T-DXd becomes an option; if HER2-0, the regimen is not labeled. Flagged as not applicable pending HER2 IHC clarification.

exclusion_reason: TROPION-Breast01 enrolled HR+/HER2- breast cancer, not TNBC. Patient is HR-negative TNBC, so this trial's population does not match. The TROPION-Breast02 row covers the relevant 1L mTNBC indication for Dato-DXd.
notes: TROPION-Breast01 was in HR+/HER2- mBC, OS at final analysis was not significantly improved (HR 1.01). Out of scope for this TNBC patient; covered by the TROPION-Breast02 row instead.

exclusion_reason: EPIK-B3 (NCT04251533) — phase 3 alpelisib + nab-paclitaxel in PIK3CA-mut or PTEN-loss mTNBC was terminated early due to slow recruitment and failure of Part B1 to meet the primary ORR endpoint. No peer-reviewed publication of efficacy data; not enrollable; the most directly TNBC-relevant alpelisib trial returned a negative readout, which removes alpelisib from the practical option set for this patient even though her PIK3CA-mut + PTEN-loss profile would have been the targeted subgroup.
notes: Part A recruitment halted Nov 2022; Part B1 missed primary ORR; Part B2 never initiated. No published efficacy paper to extract — only the clinicaltrials.gov record and sponsor statement. Decision-relevant only as evidence against pursuing alpelisib in TNBC even with a hotspot PIK3CA call.

exclusion_reason: NCT03990896 (Stanford talazoparib in somatic BRCA1/2-mut mBC) is an ongoing single-arm phase 2 with only an interim n=13 cohort; no peer-reviewed primary publication of efficacy or safety data yet. Trial entry on the screener row is sufficient — clinical-evidence row would duplicate the trials.jsonl entry without adding a published-evidence base to summarize.
notes: Trial-row only at this stage; no peer-reviewed clinical evidence to compile. Watch for primary publication.

exclusion_reason: Samuraciclib (CT7001) phase 1/2 TNBC monotherapy and combination data exist only as conference abstracts (2021-2023) with very small TNBC cohorts (<20 evaluable patients); no peer-reviewed primary publication of efficacy in TNBC. The mechanistic rationale for MYC-amp targeting is real but the published evidence base is too thin to support a row beyond abstract-only summarization.
notes: Abstract-only data; full TNBC publication pending. CDK7/MYC-amp mechanism remains hypothesis-generating only.

exclusion_reason: INAVO120 (Jhaveri NEJM 2024, PMID 39476340) enrolled HR+/HER2- + PIK3CA-mut + endocrine-resistant breast cancer with inavolisib + palbociclib + fulvestrant. Indication is HR+, not TNBC; PFS HR 0.43 cannot be extrapolated to TNBC. The inavolisib + eribulin TNBC trial (NCT07441512) is already captured on the trials.jsonl screener row; no peer-reviewed TNBC inavolisib efficacy data exist yet.
notes: Mechanism-of-action precedent in HR+; not directly applicable to TNBC and no TNBC efficacy data published. The pending inavolisib+eribulin trial is in the screener already.

intervention_label: CX-5461 (pidnarulex; G-quadruplex stabilizer / RNA Pol I inhibitor)
intervention_dose: CX-5461 IV, 10 dose levels 50-650 mg/m^2; RP2D 475 mg/m^2 on days 1, 8, 15 every 4 weeks
indication: Advanced solid tumors enriched for DNA-repair deficiency (BRCA1/2, PALB2, HRD); 19/40 breast cancer
population_detail: 40 patients over 10 dose levels; enriched for germline/somatic HRD; breast the most common tumor type (47.5%); 6 germline BRCA1 carriers. Prior systemic therapy expected.

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: 4/32 evaluable, all PRs; 3 of 4 in breast HRD carriers (2 BRCA2, 1 PALB2)

safety_summary: Dose-limiting toxicity was phototoxicity (grade 3-4 in 15%; any-grade 60%), a chemotype effect independent of the synthetic-lethal mechanism. Hematologic grade 3-4 events were uncommon (anemia 5%, neutropenia 5%).
notes: The dual HRD+MYC eligibility gate (NCT04890613) is what surfaced this drug; the published IND.231 responses cluster in BRCA2/PALB2 breast carriers, so BRCA1-specific benefit is inferred rather than shown. Later Nat Genet 2023 work flagged CX-5461 as a nonselective mutagen, a safety concern for a curative-intent candidate.

intervention_label: ART6043 (POLθ / DNA polymerase theta inhibitor) ± olaparib
intervention_dose: ART6043 oral once daily (dose per escalation) ± olaparib 300 mg PO BID
indication: Advanced solid tumors with DDR-pathway mutations (BRCA and related HRD genes)
population_detail: 61 patients: 19 monotherapy (median age 58, 37% prior PARPi), 42 ART6043 + olaparib (median age 65.5, 31% prior PARPi); median 4 prior therapies. Activity seen only in the olaparib-combination arm.
design: first-in-human phase 1/2a dose-escalation, monotherapy and olaparib-combination (NCT05898399)
effect_size: 1 confirmed PR + 1 unconfirmed CR across 42 combination patients; 1 PSA response

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: monotherapy arm showed no confirmed responses

safety_summary: The sponsor described the monotherapy tolerability as favorable, with no toxicity beyond olaparib's when combined; PK supports once-daily oral dosing with no ART6043-olaparib drug interaction. Per-term grade 3+ rates not released in the ESMO press summary.
notes: ESMO 2025 oral presentation (Yap); no peer-reviewed paper and no per-term AE table released, so toxicities[] left empty — abstract-level press summary only. FDA Fast Track (Feb 2026) for gBRCA HER2-negative breast cancer and a randomized phase 2 (POLKA) in that population make this the most advanced POLθ program for the BRCA1 axis; not a 1L option (washout expected).

intervention_dose: Novobiocin sodium oral, 5-days-on/2-days-off, dose per escalation
indication: Solid tumors with pathogenic HR/DDR-gene mutation (BRCA1/2, PALB2, RAD51C/D, ATM and others)
population_detail: PARP-inhibitor-naive or -resistant HR/DDR-altered solid tumors; germline-only testing accepted. Tumors where a PARPi is standard of care require prior PARPi exposure.
notes: Repurposed antibiotic acting on the POLθ ATPase; NCI-sponsored dose-finding still recruiting, no efficacy or safety readout published, so the row anchors mechanism only. The gate names BRCA1 with germline testing accepted; a somatic-only BRCA1 call could keep her PARP-naive-eligible where a germline call would require prior PARPi first.

intervention_dose: SYN818 oral, dose per escalation
indication: Advanced solid tumors with BRCA mutation or HR-pathway deficiency
population_detail: BRCA mutation or other HR-pathway deficiency by NGS; standard-of-care must be exhausted, placing it well past a treatment-naive 1L slot.
notes: Third distinct POLθ program on the BRCA1 axis alongside ART6043 and novobiocin; no clinical data published, mechanism-only row. Requires exhausted standard-of-care, so informational for the DDR pipeline rather than a near-term option for a 1L patient.

intervention_dose: Saruparib 60 mg PO daily (dose-expansion; 20-140 mg escalation range)
indication: Advanced HER2-negative breast, ovarian, pancreatic, prostate cancer with BRCA1/2, PALB2, or RAD51C/D mutation
population_detail: PETRA trial, 306 patients across four tumor types; heavily pretreated HER2-negative breast cancer (both HR+ and TNBC) in the breast subset; 31 breast patients at 60 mg.

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: 80% CI reported; HR+ and TNBC both included

safety_summary: Generally well tolerated with a wide therapeutic index; most adverse events grade 1-2 and less hematologic toxicity than approved PARP1/2 inhibitors. Per-term grade 3+ table not in the conference abstract.
notes: AACR 2024 presentation (Yap); no peer-reviewed clinical paper yet, so identifiers null and toxicities[] empty (abstract lacks the per-term AE table). The distinct PMID 39187844 is a preclinical model paper, not this trial. Strongest published evidence for the PARP1-selective class that HS-10502 belongs to; breast subset mixes HR+ and TNBC, so read as cross-subtype class precedent for the BRCA1 axis rather than a TNBC-specific estimate.

intervention_dose: HS-10502 oral, dose per escalation
indication: Advanced HER2-negative breast cancer (and other solid tumors) with HRR-gene mutation or HRD
population_detail: Dedicated HRR-mutant HER2-negative breast cohort (BRCA1/2 qualifying); prior standard therapy required, so a later-line slot for a treatment-naive patient.
notes: PARP1-selective agent designed to spare the hematologic toxicity that limits olaparib and talazoparib; no efficacy or safety readout published, mechanism-only row. Class efficacy precedent sits in the saruparib PETRA row; the HRR-mutant HER2-negative breast cohort matches her BRCA1 status directly.

intervention_label: RLY-2608 (zovegalisib; mutant-selective allosteric PI3Kα inhibitor) + fulvestrant
intervention_dose: RLY-2608 oral (dose per escalation) + standard-dose fulvestrant
indication: PIK3CA-mutant HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer
population_detail: ReDiscover trial; 31 response-evaluable PIK3CA-mutant HR+/HER2- breast patients on the fulvestrant combination. HR+ population — not TNBC.

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: RECIST 1.1; 74.2% had radiographic tumor reduction; median TTR 8 wk

safety_summary: Treatment-related adverse events mostly low-grade, manageable and reversible; the mutant-selective design spares much of the hyperglycemia and rash that limit alpelisib. Per-term grade 3+ rates not in the abstract.
notes: ASCO 2025 / SABCS abstract; no peer-reviewed clinical paper, identifiers null and toxicities[] empty (no per-term AE table in abstract). Efficacy is in PIK3CA-mutant HR+/HER2- disease with fulvestrant, so it is cross-subtype precedent for the patient's PIK3CA feature in TNBC, where a fulvestrant partner does not apply. Actionability hinges on confirming her PIK3CA variant is a recognized oncogenic hotspot (pending).

intervention_dose: STX-478 monotherapy 20-160 mg PO daily; MTD 100 mg daily
indication: PIK3CA-mutant advanced solid tumors and HR+/HER2- breast cancer
population_detail: 61 patients (29 HR+/HER2- breast, 32 other solid tumors); 52% pre-diabetic/diabetic; 41% of breast patients had prior PI3K-pathway inhibitor; median 3 prior lines.
safety_summary: MTD 100 mg daily; PI3Kα-WT class effects (hyperglycemia 23%, diarrhea, rash) were grade 1-2, a cleaner profile than alpelisib whose monotherapy ORR is 4-6%. Fatigue 30%, nausea 20% all-grade.

toxicities.notes: grade 1-2; WT PI3Kα class effect, milder than alpelisib

notes: ESMO 2024 LBA27; conference abstract, no peer-reviewed clinical paper so identifiers null. Reported ORR is all-comers (21%) and HR+ breast (23%); no TNBC-specific estimate, so this is cross-subtype precedent for the PIK3CA feature. Complements RLY-2608 as a second mutant-selective PI3Kα program with a favorable metabolic-toxicity profile.

intervention_dose: Olaparib 300 mg PO BID continuous + ceralasertib 160 mg PO daily on days 1-7 of a 28-day cycle
indication: Triple-negative advanced breast cancer
population_detail: plasmaMATCH Cohort E; 70 evaluable mTNBC patients, mostly HRR-wildtype (73% no germline/somatic BRCA), 14% germline BRCA1/2, 4% somatic BRCA2. 27% relapsed within 12 mo of adjuvant therapy; 56% one prior chemo line.
design: single-arm phase 2 cohort (plasmaMATCH Cohort E, CRUK/15/010)

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: 12/70; responses occurred in non-BRCA HRR-mutant and functional-HRD (RAD51-foci) tumors too

safety_summary: Grade 3+ events were led by hypertension (14%) and anemia (13%); the ATR-plus-PARP combination was deliverable in a pretreated mTNBC population. Thrombocytopenia/neutropenia rates not separately tabulated in text.
notes: TNBC-specific published evidence for the ATR + PARP axis (ceralasertib), distinct from the negative VIOLETTE randomized comparison already in the dossier. Responses in HRR-wildtype tumors support the TP53/replication-stress rationale her tumor fits (BRCA1 + TP53), not just BRCA-driven benefit. Directly relevant to the recruiting olaparib+ceralasertib arm (NCT04090567) and the ATRiBRAVE ceralasertib-priming design.

intervention_dose: IDE161 oral, dose per escalation/expansion
indication: HRD-positive solid tumors (ER+/HER2- breast and ovarian expansion)
population_detail: Phase 1 expansion enriched for ER+/HER2- HRD+ breast (~10-14% of breast) and HRD+ ovarian; preliminary proof-of-concept, including a PR in a BRCA1/2 endometrial subject.
effect_size: PR in a BRCA1/2 endometrial subject; tumor shrinkage in multiple HRD patients

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.effect_size: PR in BRCA1/2 endometrial; multiple HRD shrinkage
outcomes.notes: first clinical proof-of-concept for the PARG class

notes: Included as the class-leading PARG-inhibitor precedent for DAT-2645 (the case's PARG trial has no clinical data of its own). PARG inhibition is a distinct DDR mechanism that exploits the same HRD context as PARP; the reported activity is cross-tumor (endometrial, ovarian) and ER+ breast, not TNBC. Press-release-level proof-of-concept only, no per-term safety table published.

intervention_dose: DAT-2645 tablet, dose per escalation
indication: Advanced solid tumors with BRCA1/2 loss-of-function or other DDR-pathway defects
population_detail: BRCA1/2 LOF and/or other DDR defect by validated testing; standard-of-care must have failed or be unsuitable. Prior PARPi allowed either way.
notes: The case's own PARG-inhibitor trial; not-yet-recruiting with no clinical data, so this is a mechanism-only row and the class precedent lives in the IDE161 row. PARG inhibition exploits the same HRD vulnerability her BRCA1 loss creates but is pipeline context, not a near-term 1L slot.

exclusion_reason: No trial-specific efficacy published (DETERMINE Arm 02 is an ongoing UK platform basket, NCT05770102); the TMB-high tumor-agnostic ICI evidence base is already captured by the KEYNOTE-158 pembrolizumab row in this file, and a second anti-PD-(L)1 agent on the same TMB-14 feature adds no distinct effect size. Access is UK-only.
notes: Same targetable feature (TMB-high) and mechanism (anti-PD-(L)1) as the existing pembrolizumab-tmbh KEYNOTE-158 row, which carries the published ORR. Logged for the audit trail; the DETERMINE basket is decision-relevant as an actively-recruiting TMB-anchored route but has no atezolizumab-specific readout to compile.
